title: Answer an RFP or security questionnaire
description: A review app that drafts cited answers to an RFP or security questionnaire, leaves unsupported questions blank, and requires a person to approve each answer. It starts with recorded Chat responses, so you can inspect its refusal paths before connecting it to Glean.

preview.alt: RFP Responder review screen with cited draft answers and approval controls
preview.caption: Grounded draft answers stay behind a human review gate.

run.url: the Local URL printed by the server

prerequisites: Nothing else. The walkthrough replays recorded Chat responses, so it needs no credentials and makes no network calls

Only for a live run: a Glean instance with company content indexed, a work email for sign-in or a Glean API token with the CHAT scope, and a reviewed list of document URL prefixes that may support customer-facing answers

demoQueries.expectedBehavior: Click Try the bundled sample, then Confirm and draft answers. The app parses 20 rows across 4 tabs, merges 1 exact duplicate, and asks 19 questions. The review summary shows 10 strongly grounded answers, 2 weak answers to verify, and 8 questions that need a subject matter expert. SEC-01 and SEC-02 have cited drafts.

demoQueries.query: Check what happens when the evidence does not support an answer
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: After drafting the bundled sample, ACC-04 and CMP-01 show no draft answer and say that the question needs a subject matter expert. The rows have no citations and offer assignment to a subject matter expert.

demoQueries.query: Review an answer backed by weak evidence
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: After drafting the bundled sample, ACC-02 and ACC-03 have draft answers but appear in the weak evidence bucket. Their evidence notes explain that a person must verify the source before accepting the answer.

demoQueries.query: Compare a live questionnaire run with a colleague who has narrower access
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: In separate live runs, each person signs in as themselves and uploads the same questionnaire. A row backed only by a document the second person cannot access stays blank and needs a subject matter expert. The app does not impersonate either person.

steps.title: Copy the project onto your machine
steps.description: Creates an rfp-responder folder containing the local server, review app, sample questionnaire, and recorded Chat responses. Stay in the same parent directory for the remaining commands.

steps.title: Install dependencies
steps.description: Installs the packages for the TypeScript server. Everything runs on your machine, and nothing is deployed.

steps.title: See what it refuses before connecting anything
steps.description: Replays the recorded responses through the full questionnaire and checks that every draft has a citation, unsupported rows stay blank, weak evidence is flagged, and export stays behind approval. The command needs no credentials and makes no network calls.

steps.title: Open the review app
steps.description: Starts the local server and prints a Local URL. Open that URL in a browser. The app uses the same recorded responses, so there is nothing to sign in to.

steps.title: Load the sample and check the refusals
steps.description: Click Try the bundled sample, then Confirm and draft answers. The app parses 20 rows and merges the exact SSO duplicate before drafting 19 questions. SEC-01 and SEC-02 get cited answers. ACC-02 and ACC-03 are marked weak. ACC-04 and CMP-01 stay blank and need a subject matter expert.

aiPrompt: Build the RFP responder from the deterministic scaffold and start with its recorded Chat responses. Parse every questionnaire tab, merge only exact duplicates, and call Chat once per unique question with evidence-only instructions. Classify citation topicality separately from approval for external use. Never render an uncited draft; route unsupported rows to a subject matter expert. Preserve the original questionnaire structure, require explicit approval before export, and record the approval. Treat live mode as a later adaptation that uses experimental Platform Chat and requires reviewed source URL prefixes.
llmContext: Use the recorded responses for the default run. Live mode uses experimental Platform Chat through glean.chat.create with stream:false, store:false, and X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true, and requires RFP_APPROVED_SOURCE_PREFIXES. Read ASSISTANT OUTPUT_TEXT content and citations from annotations[].sources, preserving annotations[].snippets for grounding. Merge only exact duplicate questions. Classify citation topicality separately from approval for external use. Every answer requires a citation, and unsupported rows remain blank with needs-sme status. In live mode, use the caller's credential as the permission boundary. Retry empty chat output and keep export behind explicit human approval with an audit log.

codeAssets.description: Parse and deduplicate, make batched Chat calls, review evidence, approve answers, and preserve the questionnaire structure on export

content.problem:
A security questionnaire arrives with 200 rows. The answers exist in last quarter's SOC 2 report, a policy document, or the response you sent another customer. Someone spends a week finding them again.

Drafting is not the dangerous part. A fluent answer with no supporting evidence can reach a customer's document over your signature. This app makes that failure visible. Questions with approved evidence get cited drafts. Questions with weak evidence are flagged for verification. Questions with no evidence stay blank and go to a subject matter expert. A person approves each answer before export.

The default walkthrough uses recorded responses, so you can watch each path without credentials. Live mode runs as the signed-in person and limits customer-facing drafts to reviewed source URL prefixes.
takeItFurther: Add an xlsx and docx reader so real questionnaires can be uploaded directly. The parser here reads CSV to keep the evidence and approval logic legible.
Write answers back into the source document with a custom tool instead of exporting, keeping the confirm step and the approval log.
Give the answer library its own access control before sharing it across a team. It's a cache of retrieved content, so it can leak across the permission boundary the rest of the app respects.
Route "needs SME" rows to their owners automatically and track which ones came back. The assignment field here does not send a message.

guardrails.title: Merge only exact duplicates
guardrails.rule: Similarity may rank possible duplicates for review, but must never merge security controls automatically.

guardrails.title: Topicality is not approval
guardrails.rule: A source must be both relevant and explicitly approved for customer-facing use before it can support a draft.

limitations.title: Single-user permission boundary
limitations.description: The app runs as the credential owner. Multi-user deployment requires per-user authentication and authorization.
